Val Verde County, Texas Tax Sales

Val Verde County, Texas, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes and offers a structured process for individuals interested in purchasing properties. Below is a detailed overview of how tax sales are conducted in Val Verde County.

Notification and Public Notices

Val Verde County ensures transparency by providing public notices well in advance of each tax sale. These notices include important details to help buyers prepare.

The county publishes notices at least 21 days before the scheduled sale. Each notice includes the date, time, and location of the auction. Descriptions of the properties and their minimum bid amounts are clearly listed. Notices are posted on the county’s website and at the courthouse for easy access.

Check out our Auction Calendar for scheduled auctions.

Registration Requirements

Participants must register with the Val Verde County Tax Assessor-Collector’s Office before the auction. The process includes:

  • Completing a bid submission form for each property.
  • Providing a certified or cashier’s check or money order for the bid amount.
  • Ensuring all required forms and payments are submitted before the deadline.
  • Verifying registration details with the Tax Assessor-Collector’s Office.

Personal checks and credit cards are not accepted, so plan your payments accordingly.

Preparing for the Auction

Proper preparation is essential for making informed decisions during a tax sale. Follow these steps to ensure readiness:

  1. Research properties listed in the public notices, including their condition and market value.
  2. Check for liens, encumbrances, or other restrictions that could affect ownership.
  3. Visit the property, if possible, to assess its condition and verify its location.
  4. Consult with legal or real estate professionals to understand any potential risks.
  5. Familiarize yourself with the rules and guidelines provided by the county.

Auction Day Process

Val Verde County conducts tax sales as live public auctions. On auction day:

  • Bidding begins at the minimum amount required to cover delinquent taxes, penalties, and costs.
  • Bidders compete for properties until the highest bid is reached.
  • Winning bidders must pay immediately using cash or a cashier’s check.
  • County officials confirm the sale and issue receipts for payments.

Post-Auction Responsibilities

After successfully purchasing a property, buyers must fulfill several responsibilities:

  1. Collect the “Deed Without Warranty” from the Tax Assessor-Collector’s Office.
  2. Record the deed with the Val Verde County Clerk’s Office to finalize ownership.
  3. Address any outstanding title or legal issues, such as liens or encumbrances.
  4. Pay all future property taxes on time to avoid penalties or forfeiture.
  5. Seek professional guidance if needed to resolve complex property issues.

Redemption Period

Texas law provides a redemption period for former property owners. Key details include:

  • Homestead and agricultural properties have a two-year redemption period.
  • Non-homestead properties have a 180-day redemption period.
  • The former owner must pay the purchase price, additional fees, and a redemption premium.
  • The redemption premium increases to 50% for homestead properties in the second year.

Additional Information

  1. Val Verde County follows Texas Tax Code regulations for conducting tax sales.
  2. Buyers purchase properties “as-is” and take full responsibility for understanding potential risks
  3. The county provides resources to assist participants in understanding the process.
